newsitem.title: USA: US adj retail sales up 0.7 pct Aug 16 wk--Redbook.
newsitem.headline: US adj retail sales up 0.7 pct Aug 16 wk--Redbook.

text.p: U.S. seasonally adjusted retail sales rose 0.7 percent in the week ending August 16, according to the Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook Retail Average.

The Redbook Retail Average, formerly called the Redbook Retail Sales Growth Index, rose 8.4 percent compared with the same month a year ago, the report said. Adjusted retail sales rose 8.2 percent in the week ended August 16 compared with the same week a year ago, it said.
"The month-to-date is exactly on plan," Jay Meltzer, managing director of Redbook Research, told Reuters Financial Television.
"It was ahead of plan in the first week, a little under plan in the second week, and right on plan for the month-to-date."

Despite a slight dip in consumer confidence over the last few weeks, the level of confidence in the third quarter should still be stronger than the second quarter if it remains at its current pace, he said.
"I would think right now we would take this pace and go cheerfully to the bank," Meltzer added.
